category_title: Struggling readers who use speech recognition to test and confirm their own diction
minimal_context: The student is at the writing center using a speech recognition tool to dictate complete ideas.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's work on your story at the writing center. You can use the speech recognition tool to dictate your complete ideas.

STUDENT: I want to skip brainstorming and drafting. I am just going to dictate my complete ideas into the microphone.

TUTOR: Okay, go ahead and try that.

STUDENT: The speech recognition was inaccurate. It didn't type my complete idea right.

TUTOR: What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: (Deletes the entire draft) I am deleting the entire sentence and draft. To me, what I dictate is the final composition.

options.A: Engage in shared discourse and provide direct instruction in coping strategies within the writing center routine.
options.B: Implement cross-age and same-age peer tutoring for the student during the writing center dictation sessions.
options.C: Build a meaningful, affective relationship focused on the student's holistic growth, acting as a mentor and counselor.
options.D: Have the student independently rehearse their dictations before launching the speech recognition tool at the writing center.
